message.content: The sea usually looks **blue**—that’s because water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) and scatters the shorter blue wavelengths back to our eyes. In shallow or nutrient‑rich waters, the sea can take on a green or turquoise hue due to algae and suspended particles. In very deep, clear water it can even appear almost black. So while “blue” is the most common description, the actual color can vary with depth, light, and what’s floating in the water.
